hook.en: If the price of salt doubles, you still buy about the same amount. If the price of one brand of biscuits rises, you switch. Elasticity measures this difference.
hook.kn: ಉಪ್ಪಿನ ಬೆಲೆ ದುಪ್ಪಟ್ಟಾದರೂ ನೀವು ಸುಮಾರು ಅಷ್ಟೇ ಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತೀರಿ. ಒಂದು ಬ್ರ್ಯಾಂಡ್ ಬಿಸ್ಕತ್ತಿನ ಬೆಲೆ ಏರಿದರೆ ಬೇರೆಯದಕ್ಕೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತೀರಿ. ಈ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವನ್ನು ಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕತ್ವ ಅಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: If the price of salt doubles, you still buy about the same amount. If the price of one brand of biscuits rises, you switch. Elasticity measures this difference.
narration.kn: ಉಪ್ಪಿನ ಬೆಲೆ ದುಪ್ಪಟ್ಟಾದರೂ ನೀವು ಸುಮಾರು ಅಷ್ಟೇ ಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತೀರಿ. ಒಂದು ಬ್ರ್ಯಾಂಡ್ ಬಿಸ್ಕತ್ತಿನ ಬೆಲೆ ಏರಿದರೆ ಬೇರೆಯದಕ್ಕೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತೀರಿ. ಈ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವನ್ನು ಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕತ್ವ ಅಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Price elasticity of demand measures how responsive quantity demanded is to a change in the good's price: $e_D = \dfrac{\%\ \text{change in quantity demanded}}{\%\ \text{change in price}}$. Because of the law of demand it is negative; we usually compare its absolute value. Demand is elastic if $|e_D| > 1$, inelastic if $|e_D| < 1$, unitary elastic if $|e_D| = 1$, perfectly inelastic (vertical curve) if 0, and perfectly elastic (horizontal curve) if infinite.

points.en: e = 0: vertical demand; e = ∞: horizontal demand

narration.en: Price elasticity of demand is the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price. Above one is elastic, below one is inelastic.
narration.kn: ಬೇಡಿಕೆಯ ಬೆಲೆ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕತ್ವ = ಬೇಡಿಕೆಯ ಪ್ರಮಾಣದ ಶೇಕಡಾ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ÷ ಬೆಲೆಯ ಶೇಕಡಾ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ. ಒಂದಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿದ್ದರೆ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕ, ಕಡಿಮೆ ಇದ್ದರೆ ಅಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕ.

say.en: Percentage method. Price falls from 10 to 8 rupees and quantity rises from 40 to 52.
Point method on a straight line. Elasticity equals the lower segment divided by the upper segment.
Example: q equals 20 minus 2p at a price of 4. Quantity is 12, so elasticity is 2 times 4 over 12.

narration.en: Percentage method. Price falls from 10 to 8 rupees and quantity rises from 40 to 52.

title.en: Elasticity along a linear demand curve

body.en: For $q = a - bp$, $e_D = \dfrac{bp}{a - bp}$. It is not constant: it is 0 where the curve meets the quantity axis, 1 at the mid-point, greater than 1 above the mid-point and infinite where it meets the price axis. A rectangular hyperbola ($p \times q$ = constant) has unitary elasticity at every point. Geometrically, elasticity at a point = lower segment ÷ upper segment.

narration.en: On a straight-line demand curve elasticity changes from point to point: zero at the bottom, one at the middle and infinite at the top.
narration.kn: ನೇರ ರೇಖೆಯ ಬೇಡಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕತ್ವ ಬಿಂದುವಿನಿಂದ ಬಿಂದುವಿಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ: ಕೆಳಗೆ ಶೂನ್ಯ, ಮಧ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದು, ಮೇಲೆ ಅನಂತ.

body.en: Demand is more elastic when close substitutes exist, when the good is a luxury, when it takes a large share of the budget and over a longer time period. Necessities like salt are inelastic. Expenditure (p × q) and elasticity: if demand is elastic, a fall in price raises expenditure; if unitary, expenditure is unchanged; if inelastic, a fall in price lowers expenditure.

narration.en: Substitutes, luxury, budget share and time make demand more elastic. When demand is elastic, price and expenditure move in opposite directions; when inelastic, in the same direction.
narration.kn: ಪರ್ಯಾಯಗಳು, ವಿಲಾಸ ಸರಕು, ಆಯವ್ಯಯದಲ್ಲಿ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಪಾಲು ಮತ್ತು ದೀರ್ಘ ಅವಧಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕತ್ವ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕ ಬೇಡಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬೆಲೆ ಮತ್ತು ವೆಚ್ಚ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ, ಅಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದೇ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಚಲಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

problem.en: The price of a good falls from ₹10 to ₹8 and quantity demanded rises from 40 to 52 units. Find the price elasticity of demand and the change in expenditure.

steps.en: Expenditure: 10 × 40 = ₹400 before; 8 × 52 = ₹416 after. A price fall raised expenditure, as expected for elastic demand.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. The price of a good falls from ₹10 to ₹8 and quantity demanded rises from 40 to 52 units. Find the price elasticity of demand and the change in expenditure.

body.en: Inelastic: price and expenditure move IN the same direction. Elastic: they move opposite. Unitary: expenditure stays put.

narration.en: Expenditure test. Inelastic: price and expenditure move IN the same direction. Elastic: they move opposite. Unitary: expenditure stays put.

explanation.en: eD = (%Δq)/(%Δp): price falls 20%, so quantity must rise 30%, to 130.
